vaultScouting.evaluation: Watched Vero Beach QwikCut tape (#75). Taylor’s win right now is the frame + effort; polish pad level and double-team counters.
vaultScouting.comparison: Taylor comps to Kenny Clark — listed 6-4 / 313 vs Clark’s ~6-3 / 314 interior mold (height within ~1", same heavy DT frame); then matching occupy-and-disrupt tools from early tape (size-matched; not a Florida-alum default).
vaultScouting.projection: Taylor projects to develop into Florida’s DL room with Year-1 practice / early-down depth snaps, Year-2 compete for a rotational 3-tech / nose role, and Year-3+ starter upside as a two-gap interior if pad level and hand counters catch the mass.
strengths: Taylor already carries a true heavy-interior frame at 6-4 / 313 — length and mass to occupy doubles as a young DL.
Taylor shows active hands when engaging blockers in line work, using the frame to create early contact instead of catching.
Taylor plays with a steady motor through the whistle on interior reps — effort matches the size on early snaps.
vaultScouting.schemeFit: Taylor fits an even front that wants a heavy shade / 3-tech who can eat doubles, two-gap early downs, and still push the pocket as the hands catch up.
